data.name: Ondina
data.gender_notes: Ondina is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin 'ondus' meaning 'wave', and 'dare' meaning 'to dance'. In ancient Rome, Ondina was a goddess of the sea, and her name symbolized the gentle, fluid motion of the waves. In Christian tradition, Ondina is associated with the grace and beauty of the Blessed Virgin Mary. The name Ondina carries the meaning “Dancing one” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Ondina usually hope their child will grow to embody dancing one and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the gentle, fluid motion of the waves in Christian tradition, representing the grace and beauty of the Blessed Virgin Mary.
data.etymology: Ondina belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Dancing one.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ondina total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_hebrew.name: עונדינ
in_hebrew.meaning: השם עונדינ הוא שם נשי, והוא קשור לאגמים ולבריאה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם עונדינ נגזר מהמילה הלטינית 'Ondina', אשר טומאת על מקורות יווניים בשביל 'אונדיס', שפירושו 'ברייה' או 'מבחר', בעברית. בקבוצות נוצריות מסוימות, עונדינ נחשבת לצורה נשית של השם 'אונדי', שמקורו באגמים ובמים. לפי האגדה, 'אונדינ' היא אחת מה'נימפות' של האגם, ודמותה משתקפת באיכותה ובחסדה. עונדינ, הבת, מייצגת את הטבע, האהבה, והחיים, והיא מציינת את המקורות ואת העושר של האוניברסום.

in_greek.name: Ωνδίνα
in_greek.meaning: ονομάζεται Ωνδίνα, και είναι γυναίκα, που συνδέεται με τα λίμνες και την ομορφιά της φύσης
in_greek.long_meaning: το όνομα Ωνδίνα προέρχεται από τη λατινική λέξη 'Ondina', η οποία έχει ρίζες στα ελληνικά και σημαίνει 'ομορφιά', 'φύση' και 'βλαστήρ'. Σεบาง Νεοελληνικές κοινότητες, το όνομα Ωνδίνα θεωρείται ως η γυναικεία εκδοχή του ονόματος 'Ωνδής', το οποίο είναι συνδεδεμένο με τα λίμνες και τα νερό. Λόγω της ελληνικής μυθολογίας, η Ωνδίνα θεωρείται μια από τις 'Νύμφες' των λίμνων, που εκπροσωπεί την ομορφιά, την αγάπη και τη ζωή. Η Ωνδίνα, η κόρη, αντιπροσωπεύει το φυσικό περιβάλλον, την αγάπη και τη ζωή, και σηματοδοτεί την πηγή και την πλούτο του σύμπαντος.

in_latin.name: Ondina
in_latin.meaning: Ondina est nomen femininum, quod conectitur cum lacubus et naturae pulchritudine
in_latin.long_meaning: nomen Ondina derivatur a verbo Latino 'Ondina', quod habet radices in Graecum et significat 'pulchritudo', 'natura' et 'florescere'. In quibusdam communibus Christianis, Ondina est forma feminina nominis 'Ondis', quod est conectivum cum lacubus et aquae. Secundum fabulam, Ondina est una ex 'Nymphis' lacuum, qui repraesentat pulchritudinem, amorem et vitam. Ondina, filia, repraesentat naturalem mundum, amorem et vitam, et signat fontem et abundantiam universi.

in_english.name: Ondina
in_english.meaning: Ondina is a feminine given name, associated with lakes and natural beauty
in_english.long_meaning: The name Ondina is derived from the Latin word 'Ondina', which has roots in Greek and means 'beauty', 'nature', and 'to flourish'. In some Christian groups, Ondina is considered a feminine form of the name 'Ondis', which is associated with lakes and water. According to legend, Ondina is one of the 'Nymphs' of the lake, representing beauty, love, and life. Ondina, the daughter, represents the natural world, love, and life, and signifies the source and abundance of the universe.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ondina carries a sense of enchantment, as it is reminiscent of the beautiful, fluid motion of the ocean. Beyond its use as a Christian name, Ondina has also been used as the name of various characters in music, literature, and folklore -- all of whom exemplify grace, beauty, and an otherworldly presence.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Ondina is evocative of the idea of being carried along by the gentle waves of God's love and grace. It is a reminder of the beauty and power of the divine, and the fluidity of our connection to it. Additionally, as a name associated with the Blessed Virgin Mary, Ondina can be seen as a reflection of Mary's grace and goodness, and a reminder of the spiritual nurture and support she offers to us all.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ondina: Gentle wave of the divine ocean, carrying the whispers of God.

historical_references.reference: In medieval Europe, there is a legend of a water nymph named Ondine who was in love with a knight named Hector. Ondine made Hector a promise to be his wife for as long as he could repeat her name three times without pausing. Hector succeeded, but when he asked for her forgiveness for a minor transgression, he could not repeat her name correctly, and Ondine vanished, leaving him to live out his days alone. This legend is first found in the 15th century.

Another reference to Ondine comes from the opera 'L'Etoile' by Hector Berlioz, premiered in 1854. In this work, Ondine is a water nymph who marries a mortal man, Farnas, and eventually dies as she cannot live forever. This opera is based on the Medieval European legend mentioned above.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Ondina has seen a modern resurgence in various creative fields. In fashion, it's become a popular name for unique and elegant brands, such as Ondina Couture or Ondina Shoes. In music, there's a rising artist named Ondina who's gained a significant following on platforms like YouTube and Spotify for her soulful R&B tunes. Lastly, in literature, Ondina is a beloved character in a series of fantasy novels, with fans frequently sharing their favorite quotes and theories on platforms like Goodreads.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Ruth Ondina in Rome, Italy credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Ondina, which means "Dancing one". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
